body:
**Price check**
- Google Finance: ₹200.50 at 19 Nov, 3:30 pm IST (−1.27%).
- Screener: ₹200.55 close on 19 Nov.
- The two agree. Upstox showed ₹166 on 2 Nov and Kotak ₹162.5 on 30 Oct. The stock re-rated about 30% after the Q2 results and peaked at about ₹218 on 12 Nov. The 52-week range is ₹99–220.
- Recomputed: TTM PAT of ₹182 cr over about 26.2 cr shares (FV ₹1 after the 1:10 split) gives EPS of about ₹6.95 and a **reported P/E of 28.9**. Google shows 29.8, while Screener's 23.5 P/E does not reconcile with reported numbers.
- **Adjusted:** add back the ₹49 cr Q4 FY26 exceptional (a Right-of-Recompense settlement) and remove the roughly ₹13 cr post-tax US customs refund in Q2. That gives TTM PAT of about ₹218 cr and a **P/E of about 24**. Market cap is about **₹5,250 cr**. The company has zero debt and ran a buyback.

**Annual figures (₹ cr, standalone)**
| FY | Sales | OPM | PAT | ROCE | Borrowings | CFO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY22 | 1,010 | 23% | 132 | 31% | 223 | 59 |
| FY23 | 1,179 | 22% | 198 | 32% | 82 | 213 |
| FY24 | 1,222 | 21% | 156 | 28% | 18 | 221 |
| FY25 | 1,155 | 21% | 174 | 23% | 14 | 227 |
| FY26 | 1,144 | 20% | 141* | 21% | 0 | 190 |
| TTM | 1,274 | 22% | 182* | – | 0 | – |

\* Reported figures, after the ₹49 cr exceptional. Over five years, CFO is ₹910 cr against PAT of ₹801 cr.

**Quarterly figures (₹ cr)**
| Quarter | Dec-24 | Mar-25 | Jun-25 | Sep-25 | Dec-25 | Mar-26 | Jun-26 | Sep-26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 260 | 284 | 292 | 271 | 275 | 306 | 304 | 389 |
| YoY | −5% | −10% | −6% | −10% | +6% | +8% | +4% | **+43%** |
| OPM | 20% | 18% | 21% | 20% | 21% | 18% | 23% | 24%† |
| PAT | 20 | 55 | 49 | 44 | 48 | **−0** (exceptional) | 60 | 74† |

† Includes about ₹18 cr of US customs refund. **Underlying Q2 OPM is about 21%** (management's figure).
- **There is a loss quarter inside FY26.** The Mar-26 quarter was a ₹0.15 cr net loss after the exceptional item.
- Sales were flat for eight quarters, and only one quarter shows the jump. That is **a single explosive quarter, not yet a sustained step-change.**

**Shareholding**
| Holder | Dec-24 | Sep-26 | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promoter | 53.35% | 54.24% | Up, buyback effect |
| FII | 8.09% | 6.44% | Bounced from 5.40% in Jun-26 |
| **DII** | 31.62% | 25.74% | **Steady selling** |

Pledge was not independently verified.

**What drives the story**
- US tariff relief (50% → 18% or less) unlocked held-back demand. US component revenue more than doubled YoY.
- **Auto-component exports grew 89% YoY.** FY27 auto-component revenue guidance is ₹550–575 cr.
- Exports are 51% of component sales. A China+1 shift by global bearing and automotive Tier-1 suppliers is also at work.
- Bearing rings, the core business, grew only 6%.
- Freight is about 3x normal and is not passed through. Management guides FY27 OPM of 21–22%, with expansion in FY28 as freight eases.

body:
`insight:buffett-mistakes-admitted-2008-2025` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-02-28

Primary-source error log. 2008 letter: 'I made at least one major mistake of commission' - buying 'a large amount of ConocoPhillips stock when oil and gas prices were near their peak' ('the terrible timing of my purchase has cost Berkshire several billion dollars'); $244m in two Irish banks that 'appeared cheap', written down to $27m (-89%) by year-end ('unforced errors'); and errors of omission, 'sucking my thumb when new facts came in.' 2014: Tesco - 'I made a big mistake with this investment by dawdling'; after souring on management in 2013 he sold slowly; 'bad news often surfaces serially: You see a cockroach in your kitchen; as the days go by, you meet his relatives' (after-tax loss ~$444m per the letter). 1999: Dexter Shoe (bought 1993 with Berkshire stock) collapsed as ~93% of US shoes came from imports. 2024: 'During the 2019-23 period, I have used the words "mistake" or "error" 16 times'; 'The cardinal sin is delaying the correction of mistakes or what Charlie Munger called "thumb-sucking."' 2025 (Greg Abel): 'Our investment in Kraft Heinz has been disappointing ... our return has been well short of adequate'; Pilot - control delayed until 2023 by contract: 'That mistake will not happen again.' Patterns: buying commodity exposure near cyclical peaks; 'cheap' leveraged banks; slow exit when management or moat deteriorates; paying with own stock for a business whose moat is eroding. Actionable: write a sell trigger at purchase; act on the first cockroach.

Sources:
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2008ltr.pdf
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2014ltr.pdf
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1999htm.html
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2024ltr.pdf
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2025ltr.pdf
